transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Park (Redwood CSM); Liam Chen (MarinerBio Dir IT), Priya Patel (MarinerBio Head of Compliance), Omar Reyes (Cloud Architect), Nora Kim (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of MarinerBio vendor security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ style), focus on encryption/KMS, audit log evidence, SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO integration, and data residency constraints. Agreed to share SOC 2 report and KMS diagrams; schedule follow-up proof-of-evidence session.

Topics: SOC 2 evidence, KMS/HSM, key rotation logs, audit logging retention, SSO/SAML integration, data residency (EU/US), SIG section ownership, timeline for procurement.

--- Transcript (transcribed, imperfect) ---
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava, I'm the AE on this account, with Samir our solutions engineer. rough agenda, we'll walk through the sig questions you flagged, focus on encryption and audit items, then hit next steps.
[00:28] Liam (MarinerBio - Dir IT): Hey, thanks. Quick note, we have a hard procurement deadline end of month, so we need to get the evidence packet into our vendor portal asap.
[00:45] Ava: Understood. We'll prioritize SOC2 and KMS artifacts. Samir, want to start on encryption and KMS?
[00:55] Samir (Redwood SE): Sure. So Redwood uses a customer-available KMS integration or Redwood-managed keys depending on deployment. For Redwood Private (VPC/onprem) customers you can bring-your-own KMS (BYOK) via cloud KMS or HSM. For hosted customers we support Redwood-managed keys with envelope encryption and KMS-backed DEKs.
[01:20] Omar (MarinerBio - Cloud Architect): When you say HSM, is that a cloud provider HSM like CloudKMS or a dedicated HSM appliance? We need FIPS 140-2 level 3 evidence ideally.
[01:35] Samir: Good call. For hosted we use cloud provider KMS with HSM-backed wrapping (depends on region). For Private we can integrate with your on-prem HSM or an HSM tenant in the customer's cloud — we have customers who use AWS CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM. The HSM vendor details and FIPS certificates are in our encryption whitepaper, we'll attach.
[01:58] Priya (MarinerBio - Head of Compliance): And key custody? Who has access to the master keys if we bring our own?
[02:10] Samir: If BYOK, you control the root key. Redwood never has access to your customer-managed root—only wrapped data keys live in our runtime. If we manage keys, we have strict separation, role-based access, and audit logs for key access. I'll include an access control diagram. Apologies if I garbled some product names — sometimes the auto transcript says K-V cash instead of KV cache.
[02:35] Liam: (laughs) Yeah we saw that in the SIG, the wording around KV cache got weird.
[02:45] Ava: We'll make sure the SIG language is precise. Next, audit logs—retention, format, and delivery for evidence. Samir?
[02:55] Samir: Right. We capture three main audit streams: control-plane audit (deployment, config changes), admin API audit (user actions, RBAC decisions), and data-plane request logs (request metadata, model used, timestamp). For hosted, we retain operational logs for 90 days by default, with archive to cold storage for 1 year on request. For Dedicated/Private customers there's configurable retention and we can provide S3 exports or direct syslog streaming.
[03:30] Nora (MarinerBio - Procurement): We need signed attestations that logs were not tampered with — are they integrity protected?
[03:40] Samir: Audit logs are immutability-protected using append-only storage with checksums, and we can provide signed snapshots for given date ranges. We also keep an internal chain-of-custody for evidence generation. I'll add an example signed snapshot.
[03:58] Priya: For SOC 2 reporting, do you have a Type II? We need the latest report and the control mapping to the SIG questions.
[04:10] Jules (Redwood CSM): Yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II report. We'll provide the report redacted as needed and a control map that ties SOC controls to SIG/CAIQ sections. Ava will upload that.
[04:25] Liam: Great. Data residency — our processing footprint must be EU-only for EU patient data. Can Redwood pin processing region and guarantee no egress to US?
[04:40] Samir: We support region-pinning on Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted we have region routing policies but not hard legal guaranteed egress prevention unless you go Private. For strict EU residency we recommend Redwood Private in your VPC or a Dedicated EU-only pool. We'll put that recommendation in writing.
[04:58] Ava: Note: procurement asked for pricing differences if they choose Dedicated vs hosted — we'll provide that but as a follow-up.
[05:10] Nora: Yep procurement needs costs, but first compliance needs green light.
[05:18] [small crosstalk]
[05:30] Omar: On RBAC/SSO — we use Okta and SCIM. How do you map roles? Can we sync groups from Okta into your RBAC?
[05:42] Samir: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles (admin, dev, viewer, etc.). We also support attribute-based access control for finer grained policies. We keep an audit trail of SSO logins and provisioning events.
[06:05] Priya: Do you enforce just-in-time provisioning or do you prefer provisioning via SCIM?
[06:12] Samir: SCIM provisioning is the recommended path for enterprise to ensure consistent group membership. JIT can be used but SCIM + SAML gives cleaner deprovisioning and is auditable.
[06:28] Liam: For the SIG there are a handful of answers we haven't completed — particularly Crypto: key rotation cadence and key destruction. What is your standard?
[06:40] Samir: Rotation cadence: Data encryption keys rotate daily/weekly depending on workload; master key rotation is configurable but we recommend quarterly rotation for customer-managed keys and 12 months for provider-managed with rotation policies. Key destruction: if you decommission a tenant we zeroize keys and perform a destruction log; we'll provide the deletion certificate. I'll caveat that exact cadence can be set by policy on Dedicated/Private.
[07:10] Ava: There's a question about continuous monitoring and IDS/IPS telemetry — do you provide security event exports?
[07:22] Samir: Yes, we export alerts and telemetry to customer SIEMs via secure syslog or direct ingestion endpoints. We also have builtin anomaly detection for model usage spikes, rate anomalies — those can be exported as alerts.
[07:40] Priya: Can you provide example alerts and a sample of the types of detections? We need to show that to our InfoSec team.
[07:50] Samir: We'll attach sample alert payloads and a runbook of typical detections.
[08:05] [pause / typing sounds]
[08:18] Nora: About evidence delivery — in the past vendors gave us a big zip with PDFs; we need file-level hashes and an index. Will you follow that pattern?
[08:30] Jules: Yes we can produce an evidence bundle with a manifest and SHA256 hashes for each artifact, plus signed snapshots for logs. We can upload to your vendor portal or share via secure S3 link.
[08:45] Liam: One last technical deep question: you mentioned KV cache earlier, how do you protect cached token states? There was concern about cross-tenant leakage.
[08:58] Samir: Good question. KV cache is tenant-scoped and encrypted at rest with per-tenant keys; access control in the runtime prevents cross-tenant retrieval. We do continuous tests to validate isolation — I'll share a short isolation test report.
[09:18] Priya: Are there pen tests or externals?
[09:22] Samir: We do annual third-party pen tests and quarterly internal red team exercises. Reports are available under NDA — we can include the executive summary in the evidence pack.
[09:40] Ava: Competitor question: MarinerBio mentioned BigCloudAI; how do we differentiate on evidence speed?
[09:50] Jules: Practically, Redwood focuses on packaging evidence (control maps + artifacts + signed logs) in a way procurement likes — shorter turnaround for SOC2 attestations because we have a standard evidence kit. We'll send the kit.
[10:05] Liam: On SIG specifics, there's a question around key escrow and split keys — do you offer split-key solutions?
[10:15] Samir: We can support split-key arrangements via HSMs that support key wrapping with multiple custodians. It's more typical in regulated industries; we'll outline options and example architecture.
[10:32] Priya: A short question on retention: your default 90 days for operational logs — can you extend to 1 year for PCI-level customers?
[10:42] Samir: Yes for Dedicated/Private or an enterprise add-on we can extend retention and provide a read-only archive with signed indexes.
[10:52] Nora: When can we expect the SOC2 doc and the KMS diagram?
[10:56] Ava: We'll upload SOC2 and the control mapping today/tomorrow, aiming for 2026-04-16. Samir will upload diagrams by 2026-04-18.
[11:10] [longer discussion about SIG section owners, who will fill what]
[11:45] Priya: We'll take responsibility for the following SIG sections: vendor business continuity answers and certain organizational policies. We need Redwood to answer the crypto, access controls, and logging sections.
[12:00] Ava: Makes sense. We'll mark those in the shared SIG spreadsheet and add comments.
[12:12] Liam: On legal evidence for encryption in transit — do you support TLS 1.3 across all endpoints?
[12:20] Samir: Yes TLS 1.3 for all external endpoints; internal service-to-service calls have mTLS and mutual authentication. We'll attach cipher suite lists.
[12:35] Priya: Is there any shared responsibility matrix we can use for our legal team?
[12:42] Jules: Yes we have an SSA (shared security responsibilities) doc which maps features by deployment type. We'll attach it.
[12:55] Ava: Quick note about data residency enforcement — if you need legally binding residency we recommend Private/VPC; hosted region routing is best-effort and operationally reliable but not a contract-level guarantee unless on a dedicated footprint.
[13:20] Omar: We'll likely push for Dedicated EU pool for the initial pilot. Can you provide a cost delta?
[13:30] Ava: We'll follow up with pricing in procurement pack.
[13:40] [brief off-topic banter about conference schedules]
[13:55] Priya: A question on SSO audit — can we get per-user MFA enforcement logs?
[14:05] Samir: We log MFA events as part of SSO telemetry; we'll provide sample logs showing MFA statuses.
[14:18] Liam: For the evidence session, can you do a live demo of pulling a signed log snapshot and proving hash integrity? That would speed signoff.
[14:30] Ava: Yes, we've done those before. Samir can demo in the follow-up.
[14:38] Samir: I'll prepare a script and test artifacts.
[14:44] Nora: Procurement also needs a certificate of insurance and a liability clause redlines — legal will reach out separately.
[14:52] Ava: Noted. We'll route legal to our contracts team.
[15:00] [wrap-up]
[15:02] Ava: Recap — deliverables: SOC2 Type II report + control mapping (Ava) by 2026-04-16; KMS/HSM diagram, key rotation logs, key destruction proof (Samir) by 2026-04-18; schedule 45m proof-of-evidence session week of 2026-04-20 (Jules to coordinate). MarinerBio to send current SIG draft (Priya) by 2026-04-20.
[15:25] Priya: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the vendor portal ready to accept the artifacts.
[15:30] Liam: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[15:35] Ava: Thanks, we'll follow up via email with links. Buon -- sorry, bye.
